claims.claim: Severian of Gabala was the bishop of the coastal Syrian town of Gabala and lived approximately from 355 to 408/425.
He became a well‑known preacher in Constantinople around 400–404 and was a chief opponent of the Patriarch John Chrysostom.
The surviving fragments are transmitted in catenae and are preserved in the Vatican Greek manuscript 2217 as well as in Armenian, Coptic and Arabic versions.
